title: Supply Chain & Admin Officer
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Supply chain and Admin Officer for our operations in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

This role has a Fielad Office focus and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the implementation of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to the field Office operation while overseeing country activities.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Generic responsibilities


	Ensuring all the SC/Logistics processes are in line with DRC Operations Handbook. (P2P, Assets/GPEs, stocks, Fleet,
	Generators) etc.…
	Effective and efficient support to programs’ needs.
	Establish and maintain good contacts with suppliers, government offices, and other NGOs with regards to SC matters.
	Ensuring that an effective and efficient transport system is in place to support the programs
	Ensuring that all generators in the Area office are well managed, monitor and service on time
	Ensuring that all stocks in the Area office are accounted for and well managed
	Ensure proper filing system of all SC documents
	B- Specific responsibilities


Procurement:


	To manage all procurement activities at the Area office (P2P) goods, service, work within the approved threshold.
	Implement the procurement plans.
	To run the procurement process for the Area office requests and ensure it is compliant with DRC and donors’
	regulations.
	Ensure that there is a tracker to capture all requests for (RFQ, LVP, Cash, Payments, etc.…) and share with the relevant manager and TLs on weekly basis.
	Participate in the BFUs meetings and provide updates to the budget holders on timely and accurate manner.
	Ensure that accurate filing systems, with documented and supported records of supply chain activities are kept in the folders and uploaded on the SC share points for control or audit purposes.
	Timely process the payments for all completed good, service, work and send to Finance for payment.
	Ensure that logistics system in the Area is robust and flexible enough to cope with the support in case of an increase in the program activities.
	To perform Market survey on regular basis to analyze the trend and ensure that DRC gets the best value for money


 

Asset Management


	Ensure proper recording and updating of Fixed Asset register and ensure the appropriate tagging is performed for each item Asset/GPE accordingly.
	Ensure physical count of assets/GPE is conducted on time as per DRC SOP.
	Provides a monthly report on the asset condition that include disposal plans, transfer, and donation reports in the line with DRC Asset HB and the country SOP


Warehouse Management


	Ensure proper implementation of the warehouse management in accordance with warehouse management SOP and procedures. (Stock management, Bin & Stock Cards, release of goods is approved, use of Waybill, if necessary, PRV or GRN) are in place.
	Ensure that procured goods are received and meets the PO specifications
	Ensure timely dispatch of materials
	Schedule and coordinate mid-Year and Year-end inventories are performed
	Share with relevant manager and TLs the weekly stock report
	To report in monthly basis, the warehouse movement and provide suggestions when require.


Fleet/ generator management:


	Ensure proper implementation of the fleet management in accordance with fleet management policies and procedures of DRC.
	Ensure weekly movement plans are in place and used daily in fleet management to support the Area office teams.
	Maintain good records for rented vehicles such as driving and vehicles license, logbook, fuel consumption, insurance, etc.
	To report in monthly basis the fleet/ generator reports and provide proposals for cost reduction if necessary.
	Oversee fleet and generator running cost such fuel consumption, purchase and tracking and propose cost reduction.


Communication


	Maintain a regular communication channel between the supply chain and other program team on related matters for effective and efficient support.


Administration: 


	Oversee administration tasks related to office management. 
	 Coordinate the organization of field visits for external visitors in terms of accommodation and transport 
	Act as a focal point for the administration of contract agreements & liaise with lessors at the base office 
	Ensure that onboarding and exit procedures are done for all staff in coordination with the Logistics and Safety Department. 
	Ensure office monthly utility payments are paid on time. 
	Ensure the office is always cleaned and suitable for working.

title: Finance & HR officer
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Finance and HR Officer for our operations in Jigjiga, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

The Finance & HR officer is responsible for effectively managing financial and HR support functions at the field level. They ensure compliance with DRC’s policies and procedures and assist the Project Manager in enhancing internal controls and accountability. The role will support the AfD-funded H.E.R project (Hope, Empowerment, and Resilience) and long-term operations in the Benishangul Gumz Region.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Finance:


	Ensure timely and accurate payment processing for vendors, staff, and casual workers in accordance with DRC and donor requirements.
	Keep daily and monthly cash books updated, perform regular bank reconciliations, and oversee cash counts.
	Process and reconcile staff advances, making sure they are cleared promptly with proper documentation.
	Ensure all payments are accurately coded and recorded in DYN (DRC’s ERP system).
	Assist in preparing monthly financial reports and support internal and external audits.
	Make sure tax, pension, and other statutory deductions are calculated correctly and paid on time.
	Maintain an organized and auditable filing system for all financial documents (both hard and soft copies).


Human Resources:


	Support recruitment activities at the field level, including posting, screening, interviewing, and onboarding.
	Maintain accurate staff records, track leave, and manage contract documentation.
	Assist with monthly payroll inputs by providing updated leave balances and timesheets.
	Coordinate staff inductions and orientations, ensuring adherence to HR policies.
	Verify that all staff are registered with the government pension scheme and possess ID cards.
	Follow up promptly on HR-related correspondence and documentation with the Country Office HR team.


Experience and technical competencies:


	At least 3 years of relevant experience in finance and HR roles, preferably within an NGO or similar environment.
	Strong understanding of accounting principles and financial regulations.
	Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., DYN) and advanced skills in Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
	In-depth knowledge of Ethiopian labor laws and administrative procedures.
	Experience in HR practices and staff coordination is preferred.
	Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills; capable of multitasking under pressure.


 

EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	Bachelor's degree in accounting, Business Administration, Human Resources, or other related fields.


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	Fluent spoken and written English
	Proficiency in (Somali, Affan Oromo) preferred 


In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies: 

Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process. 

Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback. 

Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation. 

Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly. 

Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

We offer

Contract length: 10 Months

Contract Type: National Contract

Band: H2

Designation of Duty Station: Jigjiga, Ethiopia

Start date: 15 November 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for National employees

Application process

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than three pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered

Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.

Closing date for applications: October 20, 2026

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website drc.ngo.

Gender Equality: DRC is committed to achieving gender parity in staffing at all levels. In light of this, women candidates are particularly encouraged to apply to bridge the gender gap.
Equal Opportunities: DRC is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment based on mutual respect for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, disability status, religion, ethnic origin, colour, race, marital status, or other protected characteristics

We strongly encourage female candidates to apply for the position!

title: Finance Assistant (Readvertised)
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Finance Assistant for our operations in Humera, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

Under the supervision of the Support Service Team Leader, the Finance Assistant provides financial and administrative support to DRC operations and partners in accordance with DRC financial procedures, donor regulations, and national legislation. The role ensures accurate financial recordkeeping, cash management, payment processing, reporting, and compliance while supporting efficient finance operations.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Finance and Accounting


	Perform daily bookkeeping in accordance with the DRC Finance Handbook.
	Record financial transactions accurately in DRC Dynamics.
	Ensure transactions are posted to the correct project, budget line, and ledger accounts.
	Prepare payment vouchers, receipt vouchers, journal vouchers, and supporting documentation.
	Verify that all payments are supported by complete and approved documentation before processing.
	Maintain proper filing (electronic and physical) of financial records, including vouchers, contracts, tender documents, bank documents, and supporting schedules.
	Support month-end and year-end financial closing activities.
	Maintain routine financial records and follow established work plans.


Cash and Bank Management


	Manage petty cash according to DRC financial procedures.
	Process petty cash replenishments.
	Conduct daily and monthly cash counts and prepare cash count reports.
	Safeguard cash held in the office safe.
	Handle cash receipts and cash disbursements.
	Manage cash advances and ensure timely settlement in accordance with DRC policies.
	Process approved bank transfers and maintain proper documentation.
	Liaise with banks on routine banking activities.
	Monitor cash balances and support cash flow management.


Payment Processing


	Process approved payments accurately and on time.
	Ensure supplier, staff, statutory, and partner payments comply with DRC procedures.
	Support salary payment processing where applicable.
	Assist in remitting taxes, pension, and other statutory obligations.
	Ensure timely payment of operational expenses such as utilities when applicable.


Reporting


	Prepare monthly cash count reports.
	Support preparation of financial reports.
	Assist in collecting, reviewing, correcting, and filing partners' financial reports.
	Submit assigned financial progress and status reports.
	Support reconciliation of cash, bank, and ledger balances.


Compliance and Documentation


	Ensure compliance with DRC financial policies, donor regulations, and local legislation.
	Maintain complete audit trials for all financial transactions.
	Ensure supporting documents are properly archived and readily available for audits.
	Follow internal controls and safeguard organizational assets.


Experience and technical competencies: 


	Minimum 1–2 years of relevant finance or accounting experience.
	Previous NGO or humanitarian organization experience is an advantage.
	Experience in bookkeeping, cash management, and payment processing.
	Experience using ERP systems (preferably Microsoft Dynamics).
	Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
	Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word and PowerPoint.
	Strong organizational and planning skills.
	Good analytical and numerical skills.
	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multicultural environment.
	Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
	Ability to meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy.


EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	BA Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Management or other directly related field from University or higher education


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	Excellent skills in speaking, reading and writing English. 


In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies: 

Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process. 

Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback. 

Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation. 

Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly. 

Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

Contract length: 12 Months

Contract Type: National Contract

Band: I2 – Non-Management

Designation of Duty Station: Humera, Ethiopia

Start date:  1st November 2026
